The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.36,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of Koppalu Manoj Kumar, in the road traffic accident that took place on 01.08.2023.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:
On 01.08.2023 at 12.45 p.m. when the deceased was walking beside the road on Bengaluru-Hosur NH-44 main road, opposite to Metro station, Hebbagodi, Attibele Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru Dist., at that time, the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.
No.TN-24-AY-0136 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Koppolu Ratna Kumari vs National Ins Co Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96579251/
2 deceased, caused the accident, due to which deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

sentences.text: It is contended that, post-mortem was conducted at Oxford Medical college and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed the last rites and obsequies of the deceased by spending huge amount towards medical and funeral expenses.
3. It is stated that the deceased was working as mason and earning Rs.21,000/- per month.
The deceased was the only bread earner of their family and due to his death, the petitioners are undergoing mental shock and agony and facing great financial difficulties.
It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Lorry bearing Reg. No. TN-24-AY-0136.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
4. Inspite service of summons, the 2 nd respondent remained absent hence he was placed exparte.
Upon service of summons, 1st respondent appeared before the court through its counsel and filed written statement.
5. The 1st respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
It has denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased.
It has also denied the amount spent towards the medical and funeral expenses of the deceased.

Further admitted the issuance insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.TN-24-AY-0136 and liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy, provision of MV Act, valid and effective driving licence held by the driver of the lorry,
valid RC, permit and FC and also subject to the confirmation of Sec.64VB of the insurance Act.
Respondent also seeks protection under section 147 and 149(2) of M.V. Act.
It has also contended that owner and jurisdictional police have not complied the Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act.
It has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.

Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.
6. Based on the pleadings, this court has framed following issues:-
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 01.08.2023 at 12.45 p.m. when the deceased was walking beside the road on Bengaluru-Hosur NH-44 main road, opposite to Metro station, Hebbagodi, Attibele Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru Dist., at that time,
the driver of the lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-24-AY-0136 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased, caused the accident, due to which deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries ?
2.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Koppalu Manoj Kumar?

sentences.text: 3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation?
If so, to what extent and from whom?

4. What order or Award?
7.
In order to prove the case, 1 st petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to 11 documents.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has examined two witnesses as RW.1 and RW.2 and they got marked the documents at Ex.R1 to R3.
8. Heard the arguments.

As per final order For the following:
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1 : It is the case of the petitioners that, on 01.08.2023 at 12.45 p.m. when the deceased was walking beside the road on Bengaluru-Hosur NH-44 main road, opposite to Metro station, Hebbagodi, Attibele Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru Dist., at that time, the driver of the lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-24-AY-0136 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased, caused the accident, due to which deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
It is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of the rash and negligent act of the driver of Lorry and as such the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

11. In order to substantiate the contentions of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 stepped into the witness box and filed her affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R,
F.I.S, spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report, Inquest report, P.M. report and charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P8.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has examined Asst. RTO of Krishnagiri RTO as RW.1 and he has produced Ex.R1 permit extract.

Also examined Asst. Manager of 2nd respondent insurance company as Rw.2 and he got marked authorisation letter and insurance policy at Ex.R2 and R3.
12.
This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.

Koppolu Ratna Kumari vs National Ins Co Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96579251/
4 Breach of Duty:

entities.text: Koppolu Ratna Kumari vs National Ins Co Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.

Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

13. According to the version of petitioners the accident happened on Bengaluru-Hosur NH-44 main road, opposite to Metro station, Hebbagodi, Attibele Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru Dist, when the driver of Lorry came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased who was walking on the left side of the road and caused the accident.
The Respondent No.2 who is the owner of the offending vehicle
has not filed his written statement, therefore the evidence of the petitioners is unchallenged and un-rebutted, there is no evidence to disbelieve the case of the petitioners.
14. It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2. Ex
. P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P3 being the Spot Mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 and Ex.P4 which is the sketch prepared at the time of spot mahazar, it reflects that deceased was walking on the left side of the road, the driver of Lorry in a negligent manner came in high speed and dashed against the deceased person, due to the said act deceased person fell down on the road and got injured.
If the driver of lorry drove it in a normal speed, then he would certainly avoid the accident.
Added more the contents of Ex.P5 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more even the chargesheet as per Ex.P8 was also filed as against the driver of the lorry.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P3 to 5 coupled with Ex.P8 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence driving of the Lorry driver.

15. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered Koppolu Ratna Kumari vs National Ins Co Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96579251/
5 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even in the instant case the owner of the Lorry who is the Respondent No.2 is not filed his written statement and also not cross-examined the PW1 to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the driver of Lorry and he was charge sheeted.
16. Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.

The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent driving of the offending vehicle Lorry bearing Reg.
No.TN-24-AY-0136 by its driver.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.2 and 3:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the death of Koppalu Manoj Kumar, was occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the driver of offending said Lorry.
The petitioners claim that, Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards of deceased and petitioners No.1 and 2 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that, the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners No.1 and 2 are the legal representative and legal heirs of the deceased Koppalu Manoj Kumar and they are entitled for compensation.
18. The petitioners have contended that the deceased was working as mason and earning Rs.21,000/- per month.
In order to prove the same, petitioners have not produced any documents before the court.
Therefore,considering the occupation of the deceased and year of the accident, I deem it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/- per month.
19. It is stated that the deceased was aged 35 years at the time of the accident.
The petitioners have produced adhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P11 which depicts the birth year of the deceased as 1988.

sentences.text: The accident occurred on 01.08.2023.
Hence, the age of the deceased at the time of accident is considered as 35 years.

The proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '16'.
20.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 35 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

If 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.22,400/- p.m. (Rs.16,000/- +
6,400/- i.e. 40%).
The deceased died leaving behind 2 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/3rd of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.14,934/- p.m.(Rs.22,400 - Rs.7,466 = Rs.14,934/-).
21.
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.14,934/- p.m. and the multiplier '16' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.28,67,328/- (Rs.14,934 X 12 X 16).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.28,67,328/- under the head of loss of dependency.

22. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.16,500/- towards loss to estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.44,000/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
23.

In this case, the petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 is entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of father causes great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards their father.
Therefore, petitioner No.2 is entitled for Rs.44,000/- under the head of Filial consortium.

In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.29,88,328/-.
25.
As regard the apportionment of compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that the 1st petitioner is the widow and petitioners No.2 is the son of the deceased.

Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners No. 1 and 2 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 50:50.
26.
The petitioners are claiming interest on the compensation amount.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
27. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending Lorry bearing Reg. No.
TN-24-AY-0136.
After issuance of notice respondent no.1 has appeared through its respective counsel and has filed objection statement.

Respondent No.1 insurance company has seriously disputed their liability by contending various grounds and prove the said contentions, the authorized officer of the company are examined as RW.2 and he got marked insurance copy at Ex.R3.

The respondent No.1 main contention is that during the period of accident offending Lorry bearing No.TN-24-AY-0136 was not having valid permit to ply in the Karnataka State therefore they not liable to pay the compensation.

In support of their contention the Respondent No.1 has examined the one witness namely Neharuji who is the Assistant RTO of Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu, and relied on Ex.R1 which was the permit Extract of the vehicle Registration No. TN-24-AY-0136.
As per this document the offending Lorry having permit for a period from 30.05.2022 to 29.05.2027 throughout Tamil Nadu State.
In the cross- examination Rw1 has stated that "I don't know whether Lorry has brought the National permit or Karnataka State permit".
Respondent No.1 has also examined its Asst. Manager as RW.3 and he has got marked Ex.R2 and R3 document.
RW2 in his cross examination stated that "They have not done to any correspondence with the RTO to know whether offending lorry is having State permit or National Permit.

Lorry is insured with their Koppolu Ratna Kumari vs National Ins Co Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96579251/
8 insurance company".

entities.text: Koppolu Ratna Kumari vs National Ins Co Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore the said deposition of the Rw1 and RW2 makes it clear that they have not inquired whether the offending vehicle has taken temporary permit or not and there might be chances of obtaining the temporary permit to enter another State in the check post by paying the extra fine amount.
28. This Respondent in his objection statement taken the contention that driver of the Lorry was not having driving licence, but police have not charge sheeted for the offence under the IMV Act.
Mere denial is not sufficient to prove the defence raised in the objection statement.

Except oral testimony,
respondent No.1 has not produced any other documentary evidence to prove their contentions.
Further, in order to prove that there violation of policy condition, no evidence has been adduced before this court.
Hence, from the evidence available on record it can be held that the policy was in force for which insurance company is liable to indemnify the owner.
It is not in dispute that 2nd respondent is the owner and 1st respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondents have not dis-proved the case of the petitioner and breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, 2 nd respondent being the owner and 1st respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 1st respondent shall indemnify the 2nd respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 in the Affirmative and issued No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.

29. Issue No.4: In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.29,88,328/-(Rupees Twenty nine lakhs eighty eight thousand three hundred and twenty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 50% Petitioner No.2 - 50% Further it is ordered that, 40% of the amount fallen to the share of the petitioners No.1 is ordered to be deposited in any nationalized bank for a period of 2 years in her name and remaining 60% of the amount is ordered to be released in her favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.

The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioner No.2 is ordered to be deposited in his name vide Fixed Deposit till he attains the age of majority, at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioner with liberty to the petitioner No.1 to draw periodical Koppolu Ratna Kumari vs National Ins Co Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96579251/

The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.36,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of Koppalu Manoj Kumar, in the road traffic accident that took place on 01.08.2023.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.

15. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered Koppolu Ratna Kumari vs National Ins Co Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96579251/
5 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
Even in the instant case the owner of the Lorry who is the Respondent No.2 is not filed his written statement and also not cross-examined the PW1 to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the driver of Lorry and he was charge sheeted.
Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners No.1 and 2 are the legal representative and legal heirs of the deceased Koppalu Manoj Kumar and they are entitled for compensation.

ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.29,88,328/-(Rupees Twenty nine lakhs eighty eight thousand three hundred and twenty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 50% Petitioner No.2 - 50% Further it is ordered that, 40% of the amount fallen to the share of the petitioners No.1 is ordered to be deposited in any nationalized bank for a period of 2 years in her name and remaining 60% of the amount is ordered to be released in her favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
